questions.stem: What is the pH of a 0.01 mol/dm3 solution of hydrochloric acid?
questions.explanation: Hydrochloric acid is strong and monobasic, so it ionises completely and [H+] = 0.01 = 1 x 10^-2 mol/dm3. Then pH = -log10(10^-2) = 2.

distractorRationale.a: This corresponds to a concentration of 0.1 mol/dm3, ten times greater
distractorRationale.c: The value was subtracted from 14, which converts pH to pOH and applies to alkalis
distractorRationale.d: The concentration was quoted directly instead of taking its negative logarithm

questions.stem: What colour is phenolphthalein in an alkaline solution?
questions.explanation: Phenolphthalein is colourless below about pH 8.3 and turns pink above it, so it is pink in alkali and colourless in acid. This makes it ideal for titrations in which the end point lies on the alkaline side.

distractorRationale.a: Colourless is the appearance of phenolphthalein in acidic and neutral solutions
distractorRationale.c: Yellow is the alkaline colour of methyl orange
distractorRationale.d: Red is the acidic colour of methyl orange and of litmus

questions.stem: A solution of pH 3 compared with a solution of pH 6 is
questions.explanation: The pH scale is logarithmic, so each unit represents a factor of ten in hydrogen ion concentration. Three pH units below means 10 x 10 x 10 = 1000 times the hydrogen ion concentration, so the pH 3 solution is one thousand times more acidic.

distractorRationale.a: This treats the scale as linear with a factor of two per unit
distractorRationale.b: This reads the difference of three units as a factor of three rather than 10 cubed
distractorRationale.d: Lower pH means more acidic, not less

questions.stem: Which indicator is most suitable for titrating ethanoic acid, a weak acid, against sodium hydroxide, a strong alkali?
questions.explanation: The salt formed, sodium ethanoate, is the salt of a weak acid and a strong base, so it hydrolyses to give an alkaline solution and the equivalence point lies above pH 7. Phenolphthalein changes colour between pH 8.3 and 10.0, which falls inside the steep part of that titration curve.

distractorRationale.a: Methyl orange changes between pH 3.1 and 4.4, well before the true end point, so it would give a badly low titre
distractorRationale.c: Litmus changes gradually over a wide range and never gives a sharp end point
distractorRationale.d: An indicator is perfectly usable here; only weak acid against weak base lacks a suitable one

questions.stem: A solution has a hydrogen ion concentration of 1 x 10^-4 mol/dm3. Calculate its pH.
questions.explanation: pH = -log10[H+] = -log10(1 x 10^-4) = 4. Whenever the concentration is a clean power of ten, the pH is simply the magnitude of that power.

questions.stem: Methyl orange is the preferred indicator when titrating hydrochloric acid against sodium trioxocarbonate(IV) solution because the salt formed

options.text: is alkaline, so the end point lies above pH 7
is acidic, so the end point lies below pH 7
is neutral, so any indicator works equally well
is coloured, so phenolphthalein would be hidden

questions.explanation: Sodium chloride forms alongside carbon dioxide and water, but the solution at the equivalence point is made acidic by the dissolved carbon dioxide, since it is a strong acid reacting with a weak base. Methyl orange changes colour in the range 3.1 to 4.4, which lies within that acidic end point.

distractorRationale.a: An alkaline end point would call for phenolphthalein instead
distractorRationale.c: The end point of a strong acid against a weak base is distinctly acidic, not neutral
distractorRationale.d: Both solutions are colourless, so visibility is not the issue
